newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli shares rise on rumour of economic plan.
newsitem.headline: Israeli shares rise on rumour of economic plan.

text.p: Israeli shares rose on market rumours that the government will introduce a new economic plan in the near future, traders said.
The Treasury denied it plans any economic programme.
The benchmark Mishtanim index of the top 100 shares rose 1.58 points, or 0.85 percent, to 186.83 on an all-share turnover of 82 million shekels against 72 million on Wednesday.
The Maof 25 index rose 0.59 percent to 196.60.

"It's difficult to understand what has happened to the market. Speculators are the most active players and there are all kind of rumours in the market," said Danniella Finn, head of sales at Batucha Securities.

"One rumour is that the government plans a new economic plan which will include a devaluation of the shekel and budget cuts. Other rumours concern planned battles for control in several small-cap stocks," she said.
Africa Israel Investments plunged 8.5 percent to 452,445. Traders said the share fell as investors now believe the battle over the sale of its insurance holdings is over.

Bank Leumi said last week it raised its stake in Africa Israel to 65 percent of the voting rights. The bank purchased the shares to gain a solid majority to ensure that the spin-off of the conglomerate's insurance holdings goes through.
"The market looks good and all the technical indicators are showing the positive trend will continue. The big off-the-floor transactions made last week started this trend," a trader said.

The most active shares were Koor Industries, which fell 1.25 percent to 26,735 on volume of 4.0 million shekels; Bezeq Israel Telecom, which rose 1.0 percent to 754 on turnover of 3.8 million shekels; and Teva Pharmaceutical Industries, which gained 0.75 percent to 115,584 on volume of 2.7 million shekels.
